title: Lighthouse Backup Manifest
description: A versioned, deterministic inventory of the authoritative persistent state a Lighthouse backup covers. Records identity, classification, path, type, size, and integrity for every included item and embeds NO file contents, database rows, or secrets. This document is a human/Gateway-facing reference mirror; the AUTHORITATIVE enforcer is modules/backup_manifest.py (BackupManifest.validate()). Filenames and directory structure recorded here are themselves sensitive operational metadata.

manifest_schema_version.description: Contract version. Unknown/future versions fail closed.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 creation timestamp. One of the few deliberately time-dependent fields.

source_boundary.description: Absolute boundary authoritative state must resolve under (default /data).

inventory_complete.description: True only when every required authoritative item was present, in-boundary, and snapshottable.

entry_id.description: Deterministic identity derived from the relative payload path.

relative_path.description: Path under the payload/ root. MUST be relative — absolute paths and '..' traversal fail closed. Duplicate normalized paths fail closed.

source_path.description: Provenance only; never used to locate payload during verify/restore.

sqlite_integrity.description: Result of PRAGMA quick_check on the consistent snapshot ('ok' on success).

children.description: For directory entries: per-file relative_path/digest/size_bytes, enabling child-level verification.

$comment: The manifest never embeds file contents, database rows, secrets, keys, tokens, or environment values. It is designed so later encryption can wrap the backup payload without changing manifest semantics.
